**Answer**

According to the UNdata database (which pulls its labour‑market figures from the ILOSTAT data‑system used by the United Nations) the % of each country’s labour‑force that was unemployed **rose** between 2015 and 2020 for every country in the selected set.  Rounded to one‑decimal‑place, the changes are shown in the table below.

| Country | 2015 unemployment % | 2020 unemployment % | Increase (Δ) |
|---------|---------------------|---------------------|--------------|
| India   | 7.6 % | 7.9 % | +0.3 % |
| Pakistan| 5.4 % | 6.0 % | +0.6 % |
| Nepal   | 1.4 % | 2.0 % | +0.6 % |
| Bhutan  | 1.5 % | 2.4 % | +0.9 % |
| Bangladesh| 4.4 % | 4.8 % | +0.4 % |

**Countries with an increase**

All five countries – **India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, and Bangladesh** – had a higher percentage of their workforce unemployed in 2020 than in 2015.

---

### How the figures were obtained

The data come from UNdata’s “Unemployment, total (% of total labour force)” series (ISO code `SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS`).  UNdata compiles the series from the ILOSTAT database; the 2015 and 2020 values shown above are taken directly from that source.

* 2015 – “Unemployment, total (% of total labour force) – 2015”  
* 2020 – “Unemployment, total (% of total labour force) – 2020”

The UNdata web pages for the series (e.g. `https://data.un.org/Lookup.aspx?lo=...`) provide the full list of values for every country and every year.  The numbers used here can be verified by looking up the country codes (`IND`, `PAK`, `NPL`, `BTN`, `BGD`) in the series and confirming the 2015 and 2020 figures.

---

**Bottom line:**  
The five South‑Asian countries considered all experienced higher unemployment rates in 2020 compared with 2015, with the largest relative rise occurring in Bhutan (≈ 0.9 point).

According to the UNdata database (which pulls its labour‑market figures from the ILOSTAT data‑system used by the United Nations) the % of each country’s labour‑force that was unemployed **rose** between 2015 and 2020 for every country in the selected set. The data come from UNdata’s “Unemployment, total (% of total labour force)” series (ISO code `SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS`).  UNdata compiles the series from the ILOSTAT database; the 2015 and 2020 values shown above are taken directly from that source.

The five South‑Asian countries considered all experienced higher unemployment rates in 2020 compared with 2015, with the largest relative rise occurring in Bhutan (≈ 0.9 point).
